name: Catapult
description: A procedural siege catapult that teaches force and velocity vectors as a projectile launch. Two levers compose the throw — a LAUNCH ANGLE slider tilts the throwing arm and a FORCE slider sets the release speed — and a live dotted parabola previews where the stone will land before you fire. The launch velocity vector (green, from the basket) and the constant gravity vector (red, downward) stay visible: the arc is literally their sum. Press FIRE and the arm swings, hurling a RigidBody3D ball along the predicted path under gravity.
theoreticalGrounding: Projectile motion p(t) = p0 + v0*t + 0.5*g*t^2. The release velocity v0 = launch_direction(angle) * force is the entire initial condition; gravity is constant. Horizontal motion is constant velocity, vertical motion is constant acceleration, and together they trace the parabola. A throw is an initial condition — after release, physics decides the rest.

catapult.name: Catapult
catapult.description: Procedural wooden catapult: A-frame base, torsion pivot, a long throwing arm with a basket at the tip and a counterweight at the short end. A console with ANGLE + FORCE sliders and a FIRE push-button sits in front. Changing a control retilts the arm and redraws a live predicted-trajectory parabola; FIRE swings the arm and launches a ball that follows the arc. Always-on velocity (green) and gravity (red) vector arrows with labels make the parabola = initial velocity + constant gravity legible.
catapult.qfep_connection: F_force: a throw is an initial condition. You write direction and magnitude at release; gravity, constant and given, bends the rest. The parabola is the sum of what you give and what is given.

dna.default: foresight=parabola, vectors=sum - the full dotted arc plus one velocity arrow and the gravity arrow is exactly what the 4 existing placements draw today; the component arrows are not even instantiated at this value, so the scene tree and its capture AABB are unchanged
dna.was: the predicted parabola was always the whole flight path, and the throw was always drawn as a single arrow beside a single gravity arrow - both hard-coded in _update_trajectory and _update_vector_arrows with no way to say otherwise
